Hi Samantha (and Tom),

Great to hear — glad the demo landed. High-level recap and proposed next steps below. I'm attaching a concise comparison matrix (PDF) we maintain for these evaluations.

Recap (from call):
- Acme priorities: predictable latency for user-facing features, transparent cost attribution, and early detection of quality regressions.
- Constraints: mix of short chat queries (~64 tokens) and occasional long-generation (1k+ tokens) for summarization.

What Redwood provides (short):
- Unit economics: usage-based pricing with token and embedding units; we expose token-level cost breakdowns in the Console per request and per-route.
- Latency: our p95 on similar workloads (1k token responses) on Dedicated is ~220-280ms for autoregressive sampling with KV cache warmed; on Hosted API p95 is higher and depends on instance class — details in matrix.
- Cache: KV/prefix caching reduces token cost significantly for predictable prompts; we support cross-request cache keys and TTLs.
- Observability: OOTB dashboards (per-model/per-route), request traces (span ids correlated to tokens), token-level cost, and integration hooks for Datadog/Lightstep.

Recommended small test plan (we can run together):
1) Cold-start: send a burst of 50 first-time requests across model families and record p50/p95/p99.
2) Long-gen stress: 100 requests of 1k tokens to measure sustained throughput and per-token cost.
3) Cache validation: repeat canonical prefixes across sessions to measure delta in latency and token billing.
4) Trace & alert test: trigger a synthetic quality regression (altered prompt set) and verify alert firing in Console + Datadog webhook.

Next steps:
- I'll share the attached matrix (RWD_inference_vs_hyperscaler_matrix.pdf) with the specific numbers and notes on methodology.
- Dylan will propose exact payloads for the synthetic tests and share a small harness.
- Can we schedule a 45-min session next Tue (8/18) 10am PT to run the cold-start and cache tests live?

Let me know if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Samantha — quick technical follow-up and proposed test payloads (will upload harness to the shared Drive):

Notes on comparison matrix methodology (high-level):
- Cost: we normalized token cost using the 1k-token summarization workload; hyperscaler numbers were taken from published list prices + typical infra choices (e.g., larger instance classes for sustained throughput). We also show projected cost with and without prefix caching.
- Latency: measured p50/p95 on both cold and warmed KV cache for typical batch sizes.
- Degradation handling: Redwood supports auto-fallback to smaller model variants (lower cost) on overload, and a route-level SLO fallback policy.

Proposed payloads (example):
- Cold-start: 50 unique prompts, 8 concurrent connections, payload size ~64 tokens.
- Long-gen: 100 requests of 1024 tokens, sampling temp 0.7, top-p 0.95, concurrency 16.
- Cache: 200 requests with 20 canonical prefixes repeated across sessions; measure cache hit ratio and token delta.
- Observability: include a synthetic failing prompt set that returns low ROUGE and verify Console raises a regression alert (we'll provision the alert rule).

I'll upload a small nodejs harness and a Postman collection to the Drive link in the matrix, and include a short README for how to reproduce.

—Dylan
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
